content:
From my understanding of Heyting algebras, a \ b is dual to b ⇨ a. How can we ensure to_dual translates this correctly? Just tagging SDiff and HImp as duals incorrectly translates a \ b to a ⇨ b.

cc. @Jovan Gerbscheid @Aaron Liu

Yes, I have a PR doing exactly this which has bit rotted a bit (#33543). Analogous to the SDiff and HImp dualization, we need to dualize Compl and HNot (￢) to eachother. The main pain point that was holding this back is that in boolean algebras, Compl is dual to itself (and HNot is not used there). So it is kind of unclear what the dual of Compl should be.
The obvious solution might be to just dualize compl to hnot always, and create compl versions of the hnot theorems in the case of boolean algebras

Or perhaps we could have some kind of switch for the to_dual tactic? Something like to_dual +boolean which first translates the theorem and then replaces hnot by compl and tries to prove the theorem by simpa.

Are there actually that many theorems about BooleanAlgebra and Compl that we would want to use to_dual on? One example would be docs#compl_himp and docs#compl_sdiff which would be dual to eachother.

Violeta Hernández said:

Something like to_dual +boolean which first translates the theorem and then replaces hnot by compl and tries to prove the theorem by simpa.

Hmm, this might be possible. But I think it will be too much effort to implement/maintain for the amount of benefit we'll get out of it.

So yes, I think the easiest way forward is to go for your 'obvious solution' and dualize them anyways.

I imagine we won't have that many theorems about compl, but I'm not experienced enough in boolean algebras to say if this is because of a lack of API or just because there's not that many things to be said.
I'm trying to make sense of the diff/sdiff naming convention. Do you understand the name of docs#Set.diff_diff_eq_sdiff_union ?
Surely this has to be an oversight?
And on that note, we should probably add a recommended_spelling on sdiff
I don't think there is a diff/sdiff naming convention, apart from randomness.
I think from what I've seen diff is used for sets and sdiff is used for everything else
This was my understanding as well, but Violeta's example and the things around it seem to disagree!
Doesn't sdiff mean set difference?
I think so, but it doesn't make much sense given docs#SDiff more generally makes sense in a docs#GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra.
Maybe we could just use diff throughout?
diff is a bit too ambiguous to my taste, which is why I would rather standardise to sdiff
It seems 3 years ago we had the same question: #general > diff vs. sdiff

Yaël Dillies said:

diff is a bit too ambiguous to my taste, which is why I would rather standardise to sdiff

In a vacuum I would agree, but what else could we use diff for? The finite difference operator?
docs#Subgroup.leftTransversals.diff exists

I've made #40184 to rename diff to sdiff. I'd be happy to name it either of sdiff and diff, but I went with sdiff because that is what the underlying constant is called (SDiff.sdiff).

Do we have any new tools yet for helping review gib PRs like this one that are mostly boring?

While making the PR, i found out that docs#Set.sdiff_inter_right_comm is a duplicate of docs#Set.diff_inter_right_comm.
What do you think of #40184? It's already getting merge conflicts, and I won't bother keeping up with these forever. Ideally we would have some better tooling for creating and reviewing such PRs.
I like it, thanks for doing this. Can you remove the TODO in the PR description? I'll be very happy if we discuss this, but if there is no discussion and no objection I'll merge it on Monday, say.
One declaration that I did not touch in this PR is docs#Finset.diffs, which should probably be renamed to Finset.sdiffs.
Ok, #33543 (dualizing Heyting algebras) is ready for review again.
